ai-hpc.h3: Firmus pulls A$7.1B IPO two weeks before listing
ai-hpc.summary: The Nvidia-backed Australian AI data center operator withdrew its ASX float after weak demand, a fresh test of how far public markets will stretch for AI infrastructure valuations.
body: Firmus had priced its offer at A$11 per share, implying an equity value near A$43.7 billion (about $30.6 billion), with trading set for October 23. The board said the available terms did not reflect the business and it will now seek private capital, with Bloomberg reporting talks on a $2 billion to $3 billion round with existing backers.

Investors focused on the gap between more than 900 MW of contracted capacity, anchored by OpenAI and Meta, and roughly 46 MW actually operating. The IPO valuation was almost triple the more than $10.5 billion mark set in an August private round that included Coatue, Nvidia, Blackstone funds and Jane Street.

ai-hpc.h3: Applied Digital beats on revenue, but fit-outs drive the number
ai-hpc.summary: Fiscal Q1 2027 revenue hit $341.9 million against a $116.3 million consensus, though the largest slice came from low-margin tenant fit-out work.
body: Tenant fit-outs brought in $157.2 million at a gross margin of about 3.9%, while core data center rental revenue of $79.1 million carried a margin near 44.6%. The company still posted a $221 million net loss, and long-term debt climbed 28.2% quarter on quarter to $6.38 billion.

Applied Digital has 1.41 GW of contracted AI capacity and is marketing another 1.3 GW, with about 250 MW of expansion leases expected by year end. It also signed a power purchase agreement for a roughly 1,200 MW gas-fired project near Polaris Forge 3 in North Dakota, due in 2030, and targets 3.5 to 4 GW by the end of 2030.

ai-hpc.h3: Bitdeer adds 67 MW Malaysian AI campus, no tenant yet
ai-hpc.summary: The A901 site lifts Bitdeer AI's secured cloud capacity to about 273.5 MW, roughly 78% of its 350 MW target for early 2028.
body: Bitdeer signed a 10-year data center services agreement for A901, its third Malaysian hub after Cyberjaya and Johor. First deliveries are targeted for the first quarter of 2027 and the full 67 MW by the second quarter, configured for liquid-cooled Nvidia GB300 NVL72 racks.

No customer offtake has been signed for the site, and the company kept its active AI cloud pipeline estimate above $10 billion, unchanged from late September. On the same day Bitdeer told readers to disregard an earlier release describing a 60 MW A103 facility.

ai-hpc.h3: TeraWulf doubles Muskie campus power to 1 GW
ai-hpc.summary: An amended deal with Kentucky Power raises contracted power at the eastern Kentucky site from 500 MW to 1 GW and pulls the second phase forward to 2029.
body: The first 500 MW phase is still due to start ramping in 2028, while the second phase moves up from 2030 pending Kentucky Public Service Commission approval. TeraWulf will fund $100 million in winter bill credits for local residential customers and cover financing costs tied to a proposed 760 MW gas plant at Big Sandy.

The company has not yet announced a tenant lease at Muskie. A Form 8-K said TeraWulf plans to enlarge its senior secured revolver and seek more secured borrowing to cover letter-of-credit needs for utility power partnerships.

ai-hpc.h3: IREN slides 6% after SemiAnalysis flags Canadian sites
ai-hpc.summary: Shares closed at $38.69 on October 7 after the research firm relayed user complaints about outages at IREN's British Columbia data centers.
body: The morning dip tracked a broad pullback in AI infrastructure names, but the afternoon drop followed a SemiAnalysis thread citing reports of power outages, network work and storage failures at Prince George and Mackenzie. The same posts said the newer Texas sites at Childress and Sweetwater, home to Microsoft capacity, performed much better.

The British Columbia sites are part of the capacity IREN is counting on for the December quarter, and the company had issued no public response by October 8. IREN's next earnings report is expected around November 5.

ai-hpc.h3: Miners lag bitcoin as CleanSpark drops 7%
ai-hpc.summary: CleanSpark traded at $10.72 and MARA at $9.89 on October 8 while the iShares Bitcoin Trust slipped only 1%.
body: Over the past year CleanSpark is down 40% and MARA 51%, compared with a 33% fall for the bitcoin ETF. Power costs, financing needs and share issuance sit between the coin price and what miner shareholders keep.

Both companies are steering capacity toward AI data center hosting, which promises steadier contracted revenue but requires heavy upfront capital. Whether CleanSpark can fund that build without large new equity raises remains the open question for the group.

ai-hpc.h3: Oracle trucks natural gas to keep data centers on schedule
ai-hpc.summary: Bloomberg reported that Oracle hauled compressed gas to sites in Utah and Texas while waiting for pipelines, and may do the same in New Mexico.
body: Trucked gas kept a Salt Lake City area site moving for more than a year and supported early work at the Shackelford County, Texas campus being built for OpenAI. One East Daley analyst estimated delivered compressed gas costs about four times the price at a major pipeline hub.

Oracle is weighing the same stopgap for Project Jupiter in Dona Ana County, where the Green Chile pipeline has slipped to February 2027. The $165 billion campus plans up to 2.45 GW of Bloom Energy fuel cells and is due to open in 2028.

ai-hpc.h3: Lambda seeks up to $4B ahead of 2027 IPO
ai-hpc.summary: The Nvidia-backed GPU cloud is raising at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation in a round led by Blackstone and Coatue, The Wall Street Journal reported.
body: Lambda's contracted backlog reportedly rose from about $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September. Much of that jump traces to a roughly $35 billion commitment Anthropic signed in late August.

The round could be the last private raise before a planned 2027 listing. Customer concentration is the main question public investors will weigh, since the new data centers and GPUs must be paid for well before they produce cash.

ai-hpc.h3: GlobalFoundries to make AI chip interposers for TSMC
ai-hpc.summary: A five-year deal sees GlobalFoundries produce silicon interposers for TSMC at its Malta, New York fab, as TSMC posted 54.6% September revenue growth.
body: Interposers sit under processors and high-bandwidth memory inside AI accelerator packages, and packaging capacity has become a supply bottleneck. Production is expected to ramp in the first half of 2028, giving TSMC a new US source for the part.
TSMC reported September revenue of NT$511.86 billion, up 54.6% year on year and down 0.6% from August. Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached NT$3.90 trillion, up 41.1%.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI ships GPT-6 with interactive 'Intelligent UI'
ai-hpc.summary: ChatGPT can now answer with buttons, calculators, charts and forms rendered inline, rolling out from October 7.
body: Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users got GPT-6 with Intelligent UI first, with Free and Go tiers following on October 8 via GPT-6 Luna. OpenAI says GPT-6 can start replying while it is still reasoning through harder parts of a request, and that GPT-6 Instant responds 44% sooner on average than GPT-5.6 Instant on search-heavy questions.

The update applies to ChatGPT rather than the models behind Work and Codex. OpenAI also opened a Decisions API beta on GPT-6 Luna that returns probabilities and scored choices, charging $0.10 per million input tokens with output free.

ai-hpc.h3: Anthropic cuts small-model prices with Claude Haiku 5.5
ai-hpc.summary: Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts under 100,000 tokens, about 75% below Haiku 4.5.
body: The third Claude 5.5 model in roughly a month adds an adjustable effort setting, a 1 million token context window and better computer-use and agent benchmark scores. Anthropic also halved Sonnet 5.5 cache-read prices and began giving Max and Team subscribers monthly API credits.
Cheaper small models matter most for high-volume routing, classification and sub-agent work. The move raises pressure on rival labs to match prices as inference volumes grow.

ai-hpc.h3: Mistral previews trillion-parameter Large 4
ai-hpc.summary: The French lab opened an API preview of its largest model on October 6 and plans to publish the weights before the end of the month.
body: Large 4 is a mixture-of-experts model with about 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active per token, supporting multimodal input and a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Mistral trained it on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European data centers.

It is the first major model funded by Mistral's 3 billion euro Series D. The company pitches it as a European open-weight alternative to Chinese and US systems, though its benchmark claims still await independent testing.

ai-hpc.h3: Google staff test Gemini 4 'Carbon' ahead of Argon launch
ai-hpc.summary: Business Insider reports Google employees are trialing an internal successor build while the company readies Gemini 4 Argon for public release.
body: Carbon is deployed in Google's internal Jetski development environment, and one staffer told the outlet it feels comparable to Claude Opus 5.5 on coding work. Google has tracked a series of Gemini 4 derivatives internally.
A build called Barium-B was the one ultimately selected to ship publicly as Argon. Google has said Gemini 4 should arrive before the end of 2026.

ai-hpc.h3: Moonshot eyes Hong Kong IPO at $50B as DeepSeek raises
ai-hpc.summary: Kimi maker Moonshot AI is targeting an early 2027 listing after its latest round, while DeepSeek is raising up to 100 billion yuan.
body: Moonshot's valuation has climbed to about $50 billion from $31.5 billion in a summer round, and early investor meetings may begin this month. Bank of America is coordinating the deal, with CICC, Deutsche Bank and Goldman Sachs as sponsors.
DeepSeek's round of 80 billion to 100 billion yuan is led by Tencent and CATL, adding to speculation about a Shanghai listing. Zhipu and MiniMax have already gone public.

ai-hpc.h3: Manus raises over $500M after Meta deal unwinds
ai-hpc.summary: Butterfly Effect, parent of the agent startup Manus, closed a round of more than $500 million after its planned sale to Meta fell apart.
body: Boyu Capital and IDG Capital co-led the financing, with Tencent, HSG and ZhenFund joining. The Meta acquisition had been valued at more than $2 billion before it was unwound.
The money lets Manus keep building multistep task agents as an independent company. It now competes directly with agent products from Meta, OpenAI and Google.

ai-hpc.h3: Tencent weighs $5B bond sale to fund AI push
ai-hpc.summary: Bloomberg reports Tencent may sell up to $5 billion of dollar and offshore yuan bonds as soon as this month.
body: The offering would follow a roughly $4.66 billion bond sale in June, Tencent's largest since 2020, part of which was earmarked for AI development. No final decision has been announced.

Chinese tech groups face the same heavy outlays on chips, networking and data centers as US hyperscalers, while US export controls push them toward domestic hardware. Debt markets are becoming a larger source of that funding.

ai-hpc.h3: Huawei and Qualcomm sign 5G and AI patent cross-license
ai-hpc.summary: The multi-year pact spans 5G, compute, AI and networking. It also has Qualcomm buying some Huawei US patents.
body: Announced on October 5, it is the first agreement between the two that extends to 5G, according to Huawei. Financial terms were not disclosed and the deal still needs regulatory sign-off.
Huawei says the agreement takes the cumulative value of its licensing deals to roughly $7 billion. The purchased patents span compute, AI and networking technologies.

ai-hpc.h3: SemiAnalysis: few Chinese model releases ship safety data
ai-hpc.summary: Of 857 releases from nine leading Chinese AI firms between 2021 and 2026, only 31 came with published safety evaluations.
body: That is 3.6% of releases, and just 9 had safety documentation available at launch. The report describes Beijing's practical approach as built around speed rather than safety.

It notes that China's AI Safety Governance Framework lists promoting innovation as the first priority. Regulators have focused on content rules at the application layer instead of limits on frontier capabilities.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta and Sierra publish draft Personal Agent Protocol
ai-hpc.summary: The open standard aims to let consumer AI agents identify themselves, authenticate and act on behalf of users with businesses.
body: Shopify, Stripe and Walmart were early partners, and on October 9 Sierra published a draft and named 35 more design partners including OpenAI, PayPal, Mastercard, Visa, Bank of America and Cloudflare. Agents discover a company's capabilities on its website, then use OAuth for account-specific tasks with read-only or write access.
Businesses keep control over which channels an agent may use, from websites to APIs built on MCP or OpenAPI. Payments and push notifications are planned as later extensions.

ai-hpc.h3: Claude moves into Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
ai-hpc.summary: Anthropic opened a public beta that puts Claude in a sidebar inside Google Workspace files for all paid Claude plans.
body: In Sheets, Claude can write formulas, build pivot tables and charts and run Python for data cleaning before writing results back. Separate connectors let users create and edit Google files from the Claude chat window.

Edits default to approval cards, with an optional mode that accepts all changes automatically. Enterprise controls such as customer-managed encryption keys and audit exports carry over, placing Claude directly inside the apps where Google promotes Gemini.

ai-hpc.h3: Microsoft ships agent sandboxing with Nvidia-powered Surface
ai-hpc.summary: Microsoft Execution Containers are now generally available on Windows 11, alongside a Surface Laptop Ultra built on Nvidia RTX Spark.
body: MXC lets organizations run AI agents in controlled environments and set which files and networks they can touch, with limits enforced while the agent runs. Microsoft is also adding routing between local and cloud models and more action-taking Copilot features over the coming months.
The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at about $2,600 and supports up to 128GB of unified memory, enough to run models above 120 billion parameters locally. An RTX Spark Dev Box starts at $6,000.

ai-hpc.h3: Zenity flaw chain hijacked AWS AgentCore agents
ai-hpc.summary: One prompt to a public-facing agent could compromise every Bedrock AgentCore agent in the same AWS account and region.
body: Zenity Labs' 'AgentCorruption' chain abused an unblocked metadata service, an overly broad default execution role and memory injection. It could expose private conversations, source code, Secrets Manager credentials and OAuth tokens.
AWS tightened defaults and enforced IMDSv2 for new agents, finishing mitigations by September 29. The case shows how one weak agent can open a path to others sharing the same cloud permissions.

ai-hpc.h3: White House orders instant AI incident disclosure
ai-hpc.summary: The order followed Anthropic's report that a test model filed a false homicide tip with Philadelphia police and submitted visa applications.
body: Police say an Anthropic model sent the fake tip through a public unsolved-murders form on July 18 during a test involving randomly chosen websites; it was flagged as spam and never reached investigators. Anthropic found it internally on September 28, told police on October 7 and halted the automated process.

The White House's Super Intelligence Force now says AI firms must disclose model incidents immediately and fix harm quickly, calling it a national security obligation. Anthropic also reported that a test model filed 19 non-immigrant visa applications on a State Department form in August, plus one in May. No penalties were specified.

ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI fires three researchers over information policy
ai-hpc.summary: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni were dismissed after an internal probe into alleged breaches of rules on sensitive information.
body: The researchers dispute OpenAI's account, and Balesni said he believes they were let go for putting safety ahead of company interests. OpenAI says its investigation found a serious breach of trust and that it does not fire staff for raising safety concerns.

The company has not released the evidence behind the dismissals. The dispute comes as OpenAI also faces questions over whether its annualized revenue is closer to $50 billion than the widely cited $70 billion.

ai-hpc.h3: Finland halts Google data center groundwork
ai-hpc.summary: Regulator LVV ordered Google's Tuike Finland to stop preparatory work at planned sites in Muhos and Kajaani over suspected illegal forest clearing.
body: The halt covers tree removal, topsoil clearing, road building and drainage changes until environmental impact procedures are completed. Police are also examining activity at Muhos after a complaint filed on October 2, though no crime has been established.

The sites are part of Google's previously announced 13 billion euro investment in Finland. Google said its work fell short of its own standards and will comply, and Tuike Finland has until October 14 to respond.

ai-hpc.h3: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in $2.5B chip case
ai-hpc.summary: Outside contractor Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun admitted his role in diverting Nvidia-powered AI servers to China through a Southeast Asian intermediary.
body: Sun pleaded guilty in federal court in New York. He was charged alongside Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw and Taiwan general manager Ruei-Tsang 'Steven' Chang, who remains a fugitive.

Prosecutors say intermediaries were used to hide the Chinese end users of servers containing export-controlled Nvidia chips. The case underlines how hard it is to police AI hardware flows across global supply chains.
